title: 5. Tenure and Qualifications of Rajya Sabha Members

blocks.content: The Rajya Sabha is a permanent body and not subject to dissolution, with one-third of its members retiring every second year.

items: Minimum age qualification: 30 years for Rajya Sabha versus 25 years for Lok Sabha.
The 6-year tenure of Rajya Sabha members was determined by the Representation of the People Act (1951), not explicitly detailed in the original Constitution text.
Rajya Sabha cannot be dissolved under any circumstances by the President.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The Rajya Sabha is a permanent body and is not subject to dissolution.
Members of the Rajya Sabha serve a term of six years.
One-third of the members of Rajya Sabha retire every second year.
A candidate must be a citizen of India and at least 30 years of age to qualify for Rajya Sabha membership.
Qualifications and disqualifications are governed by Article 84 of the Constitution and the Representation of the People Act, 1951.
